title: Returned Transfers on the Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
A transfer out of a Keyturn Host Payout Account that comes back unpaid puts the money back on the account on the day it returns, so the host's balance is never quietly short while a bank rejects it.

## What follows a return

Money that has come back does not go out again until the host has confirmed the deposit details, and confirming them starts the schedule's change lockout period afresh.

A host whose transfers come back the schedule's number of times in a rolling twelve months has the account suspended, and the count runs on returns rather than on the sums involved. A return of a small sum therefore weighs exactly as much toward that count as a return of a large one.

## Where the marketplace was at fault

Where the return was the marketplace's own error the fee is reversed and the return is not counted toward the suspension threshold.

| The return arose from | The fee | The suspension count |
|---|---|---|
| A rejection at the host's bank | Charged | The return counts |
| The marketplace's own error | Reversed | The return is not counted |

## A clause no longer in force

One clause of these terms has been withdrawn and is no longer in force; it is not applied:

> "The schedule's returned transfer fee is charged as its own deduction, once for each return, and it is not charged twice where one return is re-sent and returns again on details the host had already corrected."
